content: The position law is defined as lin_frac(t_i) = 1/(1+t_i^2), validated across systems 0/1/2 under k=1, point constraint, order=2; the typical error is calculated to be 1e-3 magnitude (max 0.0023 in the middle band).

There is no single ti=0.8 outlier point; the deviation significance depends on multi-point tests and is based on full-band data, so conclusions must be downgraded to an observed 0.0023 deviation, not a confirmed anomaly.

The constraint-type phase transition is determined by whether the value or the derivative is constrained: derivative constraint fixes the linear kernel and always preserves the constant kernel, so lin_frac is defined as 0 and position-independent.

The k=2 sigmaH nullification requires that order equals the kernel dimension; under order=3 the two constraints leave one residual direction, so the claimed k=2 universality loss is a definitional artifact.

sigmaH monotonicity depends on the system: it is NOT monotonic in |ti| with center minimum; sigmaH is highly sensitive to basis/seeds, whereas the lin_frac direction ratio is robust across all configurations.

Statistical robustness is based on whether the quantity is lin_frac or sigmaH: the lin_frac value is robust to basis/seeds, while sigmaH and its std are sensitive; fill data gaps with deterministic probes, do not fabricate.
The report header 'gate pass' coexisting with aggregated gate_blocked is a fixed CI-layer artifact; judgment must be based on audit.score_usage/external_verify, not treated as a scientific rejection.

The resolved questions are based on history and closed: ti=0.8 significance, seeds sensitivity and basis plateau are unconfirmed observed deviations; redirect future budget to new mechanisms instead of reopening them.
